title: Direct Air Capture Packed-Bed Lab
subtitle: Follow a CO2 adsorption front through mass and energy balances.
instructions: Predict the baseline, choose the six operating conditions, then run the 24-hour adsorption simulation.
Read the breakthrough curves and move the selected-time control through the linked concentration, loading, temperature, and rate profiles.
Change one input at a time; compare residence time, capture, and temperature, then check numerical mass closure before interpreting the result.
objectives: Trace convection, adsorption, solid loading, and heat release through the coupled process.
Distinguish an axial profile at one time from outlet breakthrough over time.
Predict how bed volume and flow alter residence time and breakthrough.
Explain why capture falls as finite sorbent capacity is used.
Interpret adsorption heat release and the assumed wall heat-transfer scenario.
Use units, limiting cases, assumptions, and mass closure to judge a numerical result responsibly.
assumptions: Dry, one-dimensional plug flow with constant velocity/properties and no dispersion, pressure drop, radial gradients, or regeneration.
Gas and solid share one local temperature; initial bed gas equals feed and the regenerated sorbent starts unloaded.
Wall material names select assumed overall heat-transfer coefficients for comparison.
Toth parameters are literature-informed, while ambient-pressure kinetic magnitude is pedagogically calibrated and not experimentally validated.
Numerical mass closure tests accounting under the model; it does not establish real DAC accuracy or permanent carbon removal.

questions.question: Why can early outlet CO2 be lower than inlet?
questions.answer: CO2 transfers from the gas into available solid capacity; it accumulates as sorbent loading rather than being destroyed.

questions.question: What generally happens when flow increases for the same bed?
questions.answer: Gas residence time falls, usually weakening capture and advancing breakthrough under the declared kinetics and horizon.

questions.question: Why does capture fall near saturation?
questions.answer: Available capacity and the forward adsorption driving term decrease as q/q_s approaches one, so more CO2 exits.

questions.question: Why can an exothermic adsorption front warm the bed?
questions.answer: Adsorption heat becomes sensible heating while convection and wall heat exchange redistribute and moderate it.

questions.question: Does excellent numerical closure prove real-unit accuracy?
questions.answer: No. Closure supports internal accounting; experimental validation still needs defensible parameters and measurements.

questions.question: What does wall material change in this module?
questions.answer: It selects a documented assumed effective heat-transfer coefficient, not a universal value determined by material identity alone.
